module

public import Mathlib.Data.ZMod.Defs

@[expose] public section

/--
A perfect difference set modulo `n` is a set `D` such that the map `(a, b) ↦ a - b` from
`D.offDiag` to `{x : ZMod n | x ≠ 0}` is a bijection.
-/
def IsPerfectDifferenceSet (D : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  D.offDiag.BijOn (fun (a, b) => (a - b : ZMod n)) {x : ZMod n | x ≠ 0}

findings.description: In FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/707.lean:100–102, the final conjunct quantifies over every n : ℕ, including 0. But ZMod 0 = ℤ, and IsPerfectDifferenceSet B 0 describes an infinite perfect difference set; B : Set ℕ is not required to be finite. Consequently the assertion is false: {1,2,4,8,13} has an infinite extension B satisfying IsPerfectDifferenceSet B 0. I constructed this extension and proved the negation of the universal non-extension assertion in /workspace/review/zero_extensions.lean, without sorry or importing any problem theorem.
findings.source_evidence: Alexeev–Mixon, arXiv:2510.19804v2, §1, theorem labelled theorem:main: {1,2,4,8,13} “does not extend to a finite perfect difference set modulo any v>0.” Section 2 explicitly states: “Every finite Sidon set can be extended to an infinite perfect difference set,” with the greedy construction. LaTeX read at https://arxiv.org/e-print/2510.19804; version information at https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.19804.
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict the final conjunct to positive moduli: `∀ (B : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ), 0 < n → A ⊆ B → ¬IsPerfectDifferenceSet B n`.

findings.description: In FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/707.lean:113–115, the unrestricted modulus again includes n = 0. The library predicate then expresses unique representation of every nonzero integer, rather than a finite cyclic perfect difference set. Hall's finite Sidon set {1,3,9,10,13} does have such an infinite extension in ℕ. A construction and a Lean proof refuting the final universal conjunct are in /workspace/review/zero_extensions.lean.
findings.source_evidence: Alexeev–Mixon, arXiv:2510.19804v2, §1, quotes Hall's conclusion that {-8,-6,0,1,4} cannot be extended to “any finite [perfect] difference set,” and translates it by 9 to {1,3,9,10,13}. Section 2 states that every finite Sidon set extends to an infinite perfect difference set, citing Hall's Theorem 3.1. Section 5 reconstructs the finite counterexample proof. https://arxiv.org/e-print/2510.19804.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the positive-modulus hypothesis: `∀ (B : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ), 0 < n → A ⊆ B → ¬IsPerfectDifferenceSet B n`.

reformulations.difference: For positive moduli, the definition uses an unrestricted Set ℕ and a bijection on its ordered off-diagonal pairs, instead of explicitly requiring a finite set of distinct residue representatives with exactly one representation of each nonzero residue.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The MapsTo component forces natural-number representatives to be distinct modulo n: two distinct congruent representatives would give a forbidden zero difference. With this injectivity, the remaining BijOn conditions are exactly unique representation by ordered pairs in the residue image. Conversely, injectivity of representatives and unique representation in the residue image yield the stated BijOn. For n > 0, injectivity into the finite type ZMod n also forces D.Finite. Both the residue-image equivalence and automatic finiteness were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean. This matches the explicit distinct-representatives requirement in Alexeev–Mixon §1.

reformulations.difference: The supporting cardinality bound is stated for all natural moduli using Set.ncard, rather than only for positive finite moduli.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For positive moduli the predicate forces finiteness, so ncard is the ordinary finite cardinality. At n = 0, no finite D can satisfy the predicate, since its finitely many differences cannot cover ℤ \ {0}. Thus any satisfying D is infinite and D.ncard = 0, making the additional bound automatic. The universally quantified bound is therefore equivalent to the same bound restricted to n > 0. This exact equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes: No independent mathematical defect was found in the sole library definition: its zero-modulus value is a coherent infinite analogue, but two consumers incorrectly use it for finite non-extension results. Checked all use sites, ordered-pair uniqueness, coercions before subtraction, automatic finiteness for positive moduli, and empty/singleton cases. Lean proves the modulus-one predicate is exactly Set.Subsingleton; computational tests verified standard examples modulo 7 and 13 and rejection of repeated residue representatives. Both scratch files compile cleanly. The two counterexample refutations depend only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, not sorryAx. Erdős 707's solved-negative status and Erdős 329's open status agree with the sources.
